email — the MixOS JMAP mail client

email (dev.mixos.email) is the reserved MixOS mail client: a pure JMAP client that speaks HTTPS to any RFC 8620/8621-shaped server, whether that is the mesh's own maild or someone else's server. It holds any number of accounts, shown as a tree in the Thunderbird style. Mail is listed, read, composed, sent, flagged, moved and deleted. Calendars, events, address books and contacts are listed, shown and created. Every action can also be done over the Bus.

Running it

email [--noded-url URL] [--service NAME]

A second launch raises the first window.

Accounts are set up in Preferences

Accounts are configured in Preferences → Apps → Email, not in the app (decision). Each account has the fields below.

FieldWhat it is
NameThe label in the tree.
Server URLThe JMAP server base (https://…, no trailing slash): maild directly, or a webd vhost that proxies /jmap.
Email addressThe login, the Basic username at the token exchange, and the default From.
PasswordKept only in the app's private secrets.conf.mix (0600). It never enters settingsd.
CA bundle pathOptional. An absolute path to a PEM bundle to trust when the server's certificate is self-issued.
EnabledOff disconnects the account and keeps it listed.
SignaturePlain text added to new drafts after a -- line.

The group also holds the default account (the compose From) and the mail options: page size (10–500, default 100), mark read on open and confirm before delete. Every change applies at once:

  • a new enabled account with a password connects;
  • a change to the URL, address or CA path reconnects;
  • a rename relabels;
  • turning an account off disconnects it;
  • a removed account's client and view go.

A settings read never deletes a password. Only Email forgets one: an account removed with email.account.remove, or an empty email.account.password.set. An account removed elsewhere (in Preferences, or by a settings reset) leaves its entry in secrets.conf.mix, unused.

settingsd omits the email group at its defaults, so a read with no accounts cannot be told apart from a settingsd that does not carry the group. When such a read arrives while accounts are shown, Email keeps them (views, connections, passwords) and says so in the status line. It stops keeping them at the next read that lists accounts, or when an account is removed through Email.

If settingsd is not running, the window opens the accounts it last saw (cached in its config) read-only, and the status line says so.

With no account the window shows Open Email Settings. An account that failed to connect, or has no password yet, shows its error, Retry and the same button.

Upgrading from the single-account version. The old config.conf.mix (schema 1, with the password inline) migrates once, losing nothing:

  1. The password is written to secrets.conf.mix, and an inline CA bundle to ca-<id>.pem beside it. Nothing else happens until that save has landed. A user name and password inside the old server URL are removed (the status line says so, without the URL).
  2. The account is added to settingsd and made the default. When settingsd already holds it under another id, the password is written under that id, and that save must land too.
  3. Only then is the file rewritten as schema 2: the window shape and the accounts cache, with no secret.

Until settingsd has taken the account, the old file stays as it was and the account works as before.

Files, in ~/.local/state/mixos/apps/email/config/:

FileHolds
config.conf.mixschema 2: split sizes, mode, selected account, collapsed tree nodes, attachment bar expansion and inline display choices, the last accounts seen
secrets.conf.mixthe passwords, by account id (0600, written only by email)
ca-<id>.pema migrated account's CA bundle

A malformed file loads defaults and is never overwritten.

The window

  • The tree (left). Each account is a root node, with its connection state and its total unread count. Under each account come:

    • its mailboxes, nested by parent, with unread counts (the inbox first, the trash last);
    • a Calendars group;
    • an Address Books group.

    Clicking a node selects its account, the matching surface and that folder, calendar or book. Nodes collapse and expand, and the state is remembered. Once the tree has focus, ↑/↓ move, ←/→ collapse and expand (or go to the parent or first child) and Enter selects.

  • The centre: the selected account's mail page (newest first, as many as the page size), its calendar's events, or its book's contacts, with a server-side filter over name, email and company. The mail page is a table of one compact row per email: Subject (with flag and attachment markers; drag its edge to widen it), From and a compact Date (the time today, the weekday this week, the day and month this year, else the full date). Unread rows are bold. Clicking a row opens it in the reader; once the list has the keyboard, ↑/↓ move the selection and open each email, and Enter opens the selected one.

  • The reader: the open email (plain text first, the HTML source when there is no plain text), event or contact. A text body written as Markdown is rendered: a text/markdown part always, and a text/plain one when the toolkit's conservative detector finds Markdown in it (a fence, a table, two headings, or two of a heading, a list, bold, inline code, a link and a block quote). Quoted replies, signatures, forwarded headers, bare URLs and ASCII art never trigger it. Rendered mail shows headings, lists and task boxes, code blocks that scroll sideways, tables, quotes and links (http, https and mailto open in the desktop's browser or mail handler; the address shows on hover). Remote images are never fetched, because they track their reader: the alt text is a link to the image. Attached image previews are described below. Raw HTML is shown as text. View › Message › Render Markdown (a tick) flips one email between the rendering and its text, either way. The choice lasts while that email is open.

    The reader opens with a toolbar of what to do with the email: Reply (its ▾ chooses with or without the quoted original), Reply All, Forward and, apart, Delete. The subject comes first, as the pane's heading, then From, To and the date. A right-click anywhere in the text opens the Message menu; attachment tiles and images have their own Open/Save menu.

  • Compose (To, Cc, Bcc, Subject, body, and From when there are several accounts), reply, reply all and forward. If the account's login (server or address) changes while a draft is open, Send waits: the dialog shows the new address and Use New Address. Mail is sent through the proven recipe: build the message, upload it, create the Email in Drafts, submit it, then file it in Sent. Sending requires maild, because the create step uses maild's extension of a top-level blobId on Email/set. A strict RFC 8621 server builds an Email from uploaded MIME with Email/import, so it refuses the send; Email/import is future work. Email sends plain text only, by design. The Markdown body goes out as text/plain, and no HTML part is ever generated. This is a security choice: HTML markup, CSS and script are attack surfaces in transit and at the reader. Do not add HTML creation (decision). The compose dialog's File menu has Open… (Ctrl+O) and Save As… (Ctrl+Shift+S). They read and write mail documents, ordinary .md files with mail-* headers and a Markdown body. Opening asks Replace / Cancel when the composer has content. Saving asks before replacing an existing file, and reports invalid headers in the composer. Reads and writes run in the background, bounded to 8 MiB. Both choosers remember their last folder this session; initially they use the XDG Documents folder, then Home if it is not configured. email.compose {document: "/home/user/message.md"} opens a composer; email.send {document: "/home/user/message.md"} deliberately sends it. account may accompany document; inline message fields may not (DOCUMENT_INLINE). From and Reply-To must match identities in that account (IDENTITY_MISMATCH); an omitted From uses its default identity. Reply-To and ordered References are written into the MIME headers. A dropped .md mail document opens a composer and never sends. Ordinary Markdown joins the attachments while composing; otherwise its format refusal appears in the status line. Local drafts remain private JSON. email.compose and email.send accept attachments: ["/home/user/report.pdf"]. Paths must be absolute, readable regular files; symlinks are followed. Compose and local drafts keep the paths, never the file contents. Restoring a draft restores its attachment paths, and Send reads their current contents in the background. Under Subject, a paperclip row shows each file's name, human-readable size and an × button to remove it, followed by the total known file size. The paperclip button is always available while editing: it opens the toolkit's multi-file chooser. The compose dialog's own Attachments menu offers Attach files… (Ctrl+Shift+A) and Remove all attachments. The chooser starts beside the last file added this session, or at Home; it supports editable paths, hidden files, Ctrl/Shift selection and keyboard navigation. Directory reads run in the background and show at most 10,000 entries. Files dropped onto the window join the open compose too. Additions keep path order and omit duplicates; invalid dropped items show an inline error. Missing, unreadable and non-regular files stay listed with their state and disable Send. Chips wrap onto further rows and long names keep room for removal. Files sharing a name include their parent directory in both the chip and its accessible remove label. An oversized encoded message disables Send; the total line shows its estimated size and the account or default limit. Files are checked when compose opens, on removal, after a failed send and just before Send, with no polling. Text edits and sender changes update the size warning from cached file sizes. A draft whose file has vanished shows it as missing on restore, keeping its path. Attached files follow the plain text part in multipart/mixed, with MIME types guessed from names and leading bytes by the shared desktop MIME database on the send worker. The estimate loads no MIME database and reads no file contents: it reserves the maximum 255-byte media type per part. It therefore has a small conservative margin (under 300 bytes per part) compared with the exact message. Base64 lines contain at most 76 characters and end in CRLF. The whole encoded message must fit the session's maxSizeUpload, or 25 MiB when the server gives none. Paths and estimated size are checked on the Bus request; Send checks the files again and checks the exact encoded size. The send worker resolves an uncertain earlier submission before reading attachments. A confirmed earlier submission is filed in Sent without sending another copy. The compose dialog still requires valid attachments before it queues a send. Sends with attachments log the caller key and attachment paths in Email's application log; these details are never added to the message. A person's Send uses window; email.execute {id:"mail.send"} uses its Bus caller. Sends triggered by toolkit input retain the caller key and drive_request_id of the input replayed on that frame, matching the separate drive-request audit line. All compose sends share the same attachment check. Passes mixing local and injected input retain the drive caller and request id, with mixed_input=true recording the ambiguity in the send audit. Other send audits use mixed_input=false. email.execute refuses mail.send when its final checks prevent a send from being queued, reporting the compose error.

  • The Message menu holds everything that acts on the open email: reply (with or without the quote), reply all, forward, star, mark read or unread, junk or not junk, move, and delete to Trash (confirmed when the settings ask). Junk moves the email into the account's Junk mailbox and Not Junk moves it from Junk back to the inbox; maild trains its spam filter on those moves (there is no junk keyword). An account without a Junk mailbox shows Junk disabled, saying so. After a delete, move or junk the reader opens the next email in the list (the previous one when it was the last). Labels follow the email (Star or Remove Star, Mark as Read or Mark as Unread). Marking an open email unread leaves it open and unread: only opening an email marks it read.

  • Attachments. An email with attachments always has a bar pinned below its scrolling body: a chevron, paperclip, count, total size and Save All. Its small menu also offers Open All for files Open allows (disabled when none qualify). The chevron or Message › Attachments expands a wrapping set of tiles with type icons, names and sizes. Hover shows the whole name; a click opens a file, or saves a Save-only file. Right-click offers Open and Save. Each tile reports saving, opening, success with its path, or a failure. The expansion is remembered across emails and restarts. Save All saves every file that can be fetched. Saving writes into your downloads directory ($XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR, the user-dirs.dirs entry, else ~/Downloads) and never replaces a file: a taken name becomes name (1).ext. Names from mail are cleaned (no paths, .., control characters or leading dots, 200 bytes at most), files are written whole and readable only by you, and the status line names where each went. Open saves into a private directory first and hands the file to the desktop's default application; programs and scripts (executables, shell scripts, .desktop files and the like) are Save only. A part the server could not decode is shown greyed. The download runs in the background; nothing is written until the whole file has arrived.

    View › Show Attachments Inline is on by default and remembered across restarts. In both rendered Markdown and source views, attached PNG, JPEG, GIF (first frame only) and WebP images appear after the text, below a filename divider. Images fit the reader width without stretching beyond their physical pixel size; click opens, right-click offers Open/Save. Loading and failed previews show a note; the file remains in the bar. Undecodable parts, SVG, other types and encoded files above 16 MiB have no preview. Downloads use the existing capped JMAP path, with at most two background download/decode jobs, image limits of 8192 × 8192 and 256 MiB decoder allocation, and textures kept only for the open email. Switching emails or turning the choice off frees the textures and drops stale results. Previews come only from attachment parts, never URLs. Received HTML continues to be shown as text.

  • Printing (Message › Print…, Ctrl+P) goes through the browser's print dialog, which also offers Save to PDF: MixOS has no print service. The email becomes one self-contained page in a private directory ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/email-print/, readable only by you), shown as the reader shows it: Markdown rendered, else the plain text. Headers (From, To, Cc, Date, Subject) come first, in the light theme on white. Nothing from the email runs or loads: its HTML is printed as text, images are their alt text (a remote image would tell the sender), and a strict Content-Security-Policy allows only the page's own style and the script that opens the dialog. The page opens in Firefox through the session launcher; without one, the status line names the file to open. Pages older than a day are removed on the next print.

  • Address completion in To, Cc and Bcc. After two characters of an address the field offers up to eight: the account's contacts (from every address book) first, then addresses it has seen (recipients of loaded Sent pages, senders of other loaded pages, kept in memory only). Only the entry being typed is completed, the one after the last , or ; outside quotes. Up/Down move, Enter or Tab take one as Name <address>, (the name quoted when it holds a comma or another special character), Escape closes the list. Addresses already in the field are left out. The contacts are looked up once typing pauses (200 ms), and only the newest lookup's answer is shown.

  • Quoted replies. A reply quotes the original's text body (a Markdown email's source; an HTML-only email's text) under an "On …, Ann wrote:" line, every line marked > (an already quoted line gains another >), with the original's signature cut at its -- line and lines never re-wrapped. The person's text and signature go above the quote. Plain text only.

  • New Event and New Contact forms. Start and end are RFC 3339 instants.

Driving it over the Bus

Service email, schema email.v1. HELP lists the commands, and app.describe gives each one with its arguments and read_only flag. account defaults to the selected account. A refusal is rc 10 with {error_code, message}, and two of the codes are kept distinct:

  • UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT: no account has that id;
  • NOT_FOUND: the account's server holds no email, mailbox, event or contact with that id.

The other codes are INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_CONNECTED, UNAVAILABLE (settingsd absent), CONFLICT, TIMEOUT (settingsd did not answer a write within 60 s), STALE (the account reconnected while the request was pending, so its answer would come from the old connection), SUPERSEDED (a newer email.open replaced this one before it loaded), MIGRATION_PENDING (the account is still moving from the old config, so its password cannot change, and it cannot be removed, until that finishes), CANCELLED (Email closed before the request ran; a write that may have run answers OUTCOME_UNKNOWN), SERVER, BUSY, UNKNOWN_COMMAND, UNKNOWN_ACTION and DISABLED.

Outgoing attachment refusals have separate codes: ATTACHMENT_RELATIVE (path is relative), ATTACHMENT_NOT_FILE (missing or not a regular file), ATTACHMENT_UNREADABLE (cannot inspect, open or read the file), and MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE (the encoded message exceeds the upload limit).

Queries that need the server answer when the server does. The window never waits on them.

CommandClassDoes
email.ping, email.info, email.actionsqueryprobe; the whole window state (no secret), including reader attachment choices and preview states; the command registry
email.accountsquerythe accounts with has_password and state, never a password
email.mailboxes {account?}querymailboxes with roles, parents and counts
email.list {account?, mailbox?, offset?, limit?, query?}queryone page, newest first, with total
email.search {account?, text, mailbox?, limit?}queryemails matching text
email.get {account?, id}queryone email's headers and text body
email.calendars, email.events {calendar?, from?, to?}, email.event.get {id}querycalendars and events
email.books, email.contacts {book?, filter?}, email.contact.get {id}queryaddress books and contacts
email.show, email.quitsystem, intentraise, close
email.execute {id}intentrun any registry command (published with origin bus), including mail.attachments and view.attachments_inline
email.mode {name}, email.refresh {account?}intentswitch surface; fetch again (a failed account reconnects)
email.account.set {id?, name, url, email, password?, ca_path?, enabled?, signature?}intentcreate or update in settingsd; answers {id} once settingsd accepts
email.account.remove {id}, email.account.default {id}intentthrough settingsd, fenced
email.account.password.set {id, password}intentwrite-only: the secrets file, then reconnect; an empty password forgets it for any account id, even one settingsd no longer holds ({forgotten})
email.account.connect {id}, email.account.select {id}intentreconnect; show
email.mailbox.select/create/rename/deleteintentcreate answers {id}
email.open {id}intentshow an email in the reader; answers once loaded
email.mark {ids, read?, flagged?}, email.move {ids, mailbox}, email.delete {ids, destroy?}intentthe list and counts refresh after
email.attachments {id}querythe email's attachments (part, name, type, size, undecodable, save_only), never their content
email.attachment.save {id, part, dir?}intentsave one attachment (into dir, absolute and existing, else the downloads directory) without replacing a file; answers {path}
email.contacts.suggest {text, limit?}queryaddress completions for text: contacts first, then addresses the account has seen; at most limit (8)
email.print {id?}intentwrite the print page (the open email by default) and open it in the browser; answers {path, opened}
email.junk {ids, junk}intentmove to the Junk mailbox (junk: true) or back to the inbox; maild trains spam or ham on the move; answers {ids, mailbox}
email.send {document?, from?, to?, cc?, bcc?, reply_to?, subject?, body?, in_reply_to?, references?, attachments?}intentsend a mail document or inline fields (To and subject required); From/Reply-To must be owned identity addresses; references is an ordered string or list; attachments are absolute paths read at send time
email.compose {document?, to?, cc?, bcc?, reply_to?, subject?, body?, in_reply_to?, references?, attachments?}intentopen a mail document or inline fields; document excludes inline fields; Send reads attachment paths
email.compose.attachment.add {paths:["/home/user/report.pdf"]}intentadd to the open compose in order, omitting duplicate paths; no compose: NOT_FOUND, sending: BUSY; relative, non-regular or unreadable paths use ATTACHMENT_RELATIVE, ATTACHMENT_NOT_FILE or ATTACHMENT_UNREADABLE; an invalid batch changes nothing; answers {compose}
email.compose.attachment.remove {path}intentremove all occurrences of the exact path from the open compose; no compose or unknown path: NOT_FOUND, sending: BUSY; answers {compose}
email.reply {id, all?}, email.forward {id, to?}intentopen the compose dialog, filled in
email.calendar.select, email.event.create/update/deleteintentcreate answers {id}; end or an ISO 8601 duration
email.book.select, email.contact.create/update/deleteintentcreate answers {id}
email.ui.*, email.window, email.window.stateinput, querythe toolkit drive commands

Every command the window runs (menu, shortcut, button or email.execute) is published on email.action.executed with how it was reached.

The compose object in email.info (also returned by email.compose and attachment removal) lists attachments: [{path, name, label, size, state}]. Sizes are raw bytes, or null when unknown; states are ready, missing, not_file, unreadable and relative. name is the plain basename; label is the text shown by the chip, including a directory qualifier when basenames collide. It also reports attachment_size (the sum of known raw file sizes), attachment_error, attachments_over_limit and sendable, matching the dialog, and send_origin: {caller_key, drive_request_id, mixed_input} after a send starts; failed sends clear that origin. Removal matches the supplied path exactly, preserving symlink paths, and updates the saved draft. UI fields remain drivable through the toolkit commands.

email.info reports how the open email is shown under each account's mail.reader: {"format": "markdown" | "plain", "auto": true | false, "attachments_expanded": false, "attachments_inline": true, "attachments": []}, where auto is false once the person (or email.execute {"id":"view.reader.markdown"}) has flipped it. The command is disabled when the open email has no text body.

The reader's attachments list contains {part, preview: {state}}, where state is none, loading, shown or failed; failures also carry reason. Non-previewable parts and disabled inline display report none. The choices are available through email.execute {"id":"mail.attachments"} and email.execute {"id":"view.attachments_inline"} and their checked state appears in email.actions. The existing mail.attachments metadata and transfer states remain available beside mail.reader.

From Mix:

send email email.accounts
send email email.list body='{"account":"acct-3f9a1c2b4d5e","mailbox":"m-inbox","limit":20}'
send email email.search body='{"text":"invoice"}'
send email email.mark body='{"ids":["E42"],"read":false}'
send email email.event.create body='{"title":"Standup","start":"2026-10-17T09:00:00+10:00","duration":"PT15M"}'
send email email.account.password.set body='{"id":"acct-3f9a1c2b4d5e","password":"…"}'

How it talks to the server

There is one HTTPS client per account. On connect, the password is exchanged for a Bearer token (POST /auth/tokens/issue) and the Session is discovered (GET /.well-known/jmap). Every method call after that carries the token. A server without the token endpoint falls back to Basic auth on every request. Requests batch their methodCalls and chain Email/query into Email/get through a ResultReference, so a list is one round trip. Every answer carries its account id and connection generation, so a late answer from one account, or from an account's earlier connection, is never applied to another.

The engine (apps/email/crates/jmap) is ported from the retired Dioxus mail client, with its faults fixed:

  • session discovery and URL templates instead of hard-coded paths;
  • real pagination;
  • Bcc carried through;
  • In-Reply-To wrapped exactly once;
  • CR/LF stripped from header inputs (header injection);
  • typed handling of method errors.

Performance workload

The recorded workload for future profiling is a 10,000-email mailbox in each of several accounts. The list renders one page (the page size) from a single query-and-get round trip, the reader fetches one email's bodies when it opens, and the tree's work grows with the mailbox count, not the email count. Nothing else scales with mailbox size.

Macro Bus commands

The shared macro Bus surface uses this process's catalogue and runner. Subscribe to <service>.macros.finished for completion, where service is the instance’s registered Bus name (for example term-1234 for a second Term instance). Commands keep the app’s canonical prefix, such as email.macros.run.

CommandArgumentsResult
email.macros.list{}Catalogue and diagnostics
email.macros.reload{}Catalogue and diagnostics
email.macros.run{id}Acceptance and run number
email.macros.status{}Current or last run
email.macros.output{}Retained output and dropped flag
email.macros.stop{}Whether termination was requested
email.macros.new{title}Create a user per-app macro; {id,title,path,scanned}, without opening an editor; scan failures add warning and preserve the file
